# dsh-workspace-mesh
**English** · 中文

Workspace **mesh** for DeepSeek Harness — a grid of
*workspaces*, not of agents.

> **Not resource remote-access.** The agent loop never leaves the machine that owns the workspace.
>

Peers exchange messages only: no remote shell, no remote file API — by design
> (SPEC.md §8, §16.6)

Peers exchange messages only: no remote shell, no remote file API — by design
> (SPEC.md §8, §16.6).
## Why

You run more than one DSH instance: a laptop, a staging box, a cloud host. Work does not spread
even

ly over them — a workspace *belongs* to one machine, and the repository, the credentials and the
lon
g-running sessions live there.

Proxying a conversation to that machine already works, and it has the right shape: the agent loop
st

ays where the files are. What is missing is the other direction — **one Lead that dispatches work
by

workspace, to the machine that owns it, and reads the result back**, without knowing which box
is w

space, to the machine that owns it, and reads the result back**, without knowing which box
is which.
[代码示例省略，未执行]
## What it does
| **Declares placement** | `assignment.yml` maps `workspaceId → nodeId`, plus the remote `cwd` a new

session owns. Static by design — no discovery, no hub process. |
| **Dispatches by workspace** | `m
esh_dispatch` creates a session on the owning machine, sends the objective, and blocks until the fin

al reply (or `dispatchTimeoutMs`). |
| **Reports, never guesses** | `mesh_list_nodes` merges the ass

ignment table with transport receipts. A peer without a receipt is `unknown` — never `online`. |
| *
*Stays out of execution** | Across the machine boundary only `session/*` and `workspace/*` calls tra

vel. |
| **Degrades, does not crash** | No peers? The plugin still loads; `mesh_dispatch` reports `u

navailable` and the other three tools keep working. |
| **Zero runtime dependencies** | Plain JSON S
chema tool definitions; cordis services are probed at runtime instead of imported from the host (SPE
definitions; cordis services are probed at runtime instead of imported from the host (SPEC §9.4). |
## Requirements

| dsh | `>=0.2.1-rc.2` — declared in `dsh.engines`, checked when the bundle loads |
| Node.js | `>=2

0` |
| Runtime dependencies | none |
| Peers | a DSH instance serving its web UI (the transport call
s `/connect` and `/api/...` there) |

### 1. Install on every node you want to address

The caller needs the plugin for the tools and the transport. A peer needs it to publish its native
w
orkspaces (`GET /api/mesh/workspaces`) and, in relay mode, to serve the handshake and relay routes.
A peer without it still works when every assignment carries a `cwd`: the transport then creates the
session in that directory.

## Credentials
| Mode | Configure | After the peer restarts | Authority on the peer |
| login token (default) | `peers[].token` | the token rotates; update it by hand | the owner's full

access |
| relay | `peers[].token` + the same `meshSecret` on both nodes | automatic re-handshake, n
othing to update | a 10-minute mesh token, five session operations |

In relay mode the caller signs `mesh-handshake:<nodeId>:<ts>:<nonce>` with the shared secret and
tra

des it for a short-lived token, so nothing depends on the rotating login token. The handshake and
re

lay routes sit below the browser fence — the caller has no cookie yet — and verify that token
themse

outes sit below the browser fence — the caller has no cookie yet — and verify that token
themselves.
Peers back off after two consecutive failures (60 s, doubling, capped at 16×) instead of hammering a
stale credential: a steady stream of 401s is exactly what a host intrusion filter bans this machine

e credential: a steady stream of 401s is exactly what a host intrusion filter bans this machine
for.
> **Keep the mesh on a trusted network.** The login token *is* the peer's owner session. Relay mode

> narrows that to five session operations, but neither mode replaces the credential layer in SPEC
>
§17, which does not exist yet (decisions.md D13).
## Model tools
| Tool | What it does |
| `mesh_list_nodes` | Roster: the assignment table merged with transport receipts, filterable by `no

deId` / `workspaceId`. |
| `mesh_status` | Local snapshot — transport, assignment table, task board

counts, lifecycle. Never calls the network. |
| `mesh_dispatch` | Dispatch a task and block for the

reply. Returns `taskId`, `target`, `state`, `result` or an `error` code. |
| `mesh_task_status` | Re
ad one task off the in-memory board (cleared when the process exits). |

Error codes: `unavailable`, `unknown-node`, `invalid-target`, `denied`, `node-offline`, `timeout`,
`

remote-failure`. Parameters, output shapes and the `replyMode` caveat:
docs/reference/tools.md.
## Settings page

The browser half registers four surfaces: a **Workspace mesh** section in Settings, a live
configura

tion card on the plugin's own page, a left-rail entry, and the workspace page that entry
opens — eve

ry reachable workspace, which machine owns it, whether that machine is online, a message
box for it,

and a read-only view of a remote session's tail. Remote workspaces are virtual there:
